name: Starter: Georgian
about: Georgian in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Georgian order.

words.ყოფნა: be (ვარ am, ხარ are, არის is, არიან are; ვიყავი, იყო, ვიყავით was, were)
words.ჩემი: my (ჩემმა: my, for the doer in the past)
words.ქონა: have a thing (მაქვს: I have, გაქვთ: you have)
words.ყოლა: have a person or a pet (მყავს: I have)
words.ნდომა: want (მინდა: I want, გინდა: you want)
words.წასვლა: go (მიდიხარ: you're going, წავალ: I'll go)
words.სწავლა: study, learn (სწავლობს: studies, ვისწავლო: that I learn)

items.text: ერთი ჩაი და ერთი წყალი, თუ შეიძლება.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: ერთი ჩაის და ერთი წყალს, თუ შეიძლება.
ერთს ჩაი და ერთს წყალი, თუ შეიძლება.

items.means: I have a brother and a sister.
Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Excuse me, how much is it?
I live in a small house.
My mother is going to the city.
Tomorrow I'll go to the city.
Where does your sister go to school?
My dad gets home from work late.
The children are playing in the yard.
The keys are on the table.
There's no milk in the fridge.
We live in the city center.
The books are on the shelf.
Yesterday we had lunch at a restaurant.
There was no bread at the store.
What do you want to drink?
I go to work by bus.
The airport is far from here.
Tomorrow I'll take a taxi to the airport.
The pharmacy is by the bank.
What does this mean in English?
On Saturday we'll go to Batumi.
We were at the beach last summer.
We're going to the movies with a friend.
I'll wait for you at the station.

concept.line: The verb often shows who: ვ- marks I (ვცხოვრობ: I live), ვ- with -თ we (ვცხოვრობთ), -ს he or she (ცხოვრობს), and -თ without ვ- you, to more than one or politely (ცხოვრობთ).
ვარ is am, ხარ are (to one person), არის is, and is can join the word before it as -ა: მე სტუდენტი ვარ (I student am), ეს ჩემი სახლია (this my house-is).

words.means: დედაა = is a mother; დედა = mother
მამაა = is a father; მამა = father

concept.line: ჩემი (my), შენი (your), მისი (his, her), ჩვენი (our) and თქვენი (your, polite) go before the noun; mom and dad often take my on the end: დედაჩემი (my mom).

words.means: მაქვს = I have; გაქვთ = you have
მყავს = to have a person or animal (also commonly a car)

concept.line: A question word goes just before the verb, and a yes-or-no question keeps its order and rises at the end: სად ცხოვრობ?

words.means: ლაპარაკობ = you speak; ვლაპარაკობ = I speak; ლაპარაკობს = speaks
მესმის = I understand; გესმის = you understand

concept.line: არ before the verb is not, and ვერ is can't: არ ვიცი (not I-know: I don't know), ვერ გავიგე (couldn't I-understood: I didn't catch that).

words.means: სახლში = in a house; სახლი = house; სახლია = is a house
ვცხოვრობ = I live; ცხოვრობ = you live; ცხოვრობს = lives
მიდიხარ = you are going; მიდის = goes; მივდივარ = I am going
მანქანა = car; მანქანაა = is a car

concept.line: მაქვს is I have a thing and მყავს I have a person or a pet, with the one you have as it is: მანქანა მაქვს (car I-have), ძმა მყავს (brother I-have); for you, გაქვს and გყავს.

words.means: ვმუშაობ = I work; ვიმუშაო = that I work
წავიდე = that I go; წავალ = I will go; წასვლა = going
